newsitem.title: GERMANY: German farm co-ops see lower 1997 grains revenue.
newsitem.headline: German farm co-ops see lower 1997 grains revenue.

text.p: German grain prices are expected to fall this year and higher sales into intervention are likely under supply pressure, the umbrella organisation of farm cooperatives (DRV) said.
In a statement issued during annual meetings, it cited falling international prices and the halving of the European Union land set-aside rate, which would result in more supplies.
DRV said higher grains, feeds and seeds prices contributed to higher 1996 turnover at the 4,681 co-ops, which market half of all German grains and oilseeds on behalf of farmers.
But revenue from potato and oilseeds sales was lower.
The coops' combined turnover in 1996 was an estimated 78.6 billion marks compared with 77.7 billion in 1995.
This included 890 cooperatives in eastern Germany with sales worth 3.30 billion marks (3.28 billion 1995).
The number of coops in 1996 declined by 4.6 percent.
